parsed.reasoning: Role type: The title is Research Engineer / Research Scientist, and the posting says the role 'sits squarely across research and engineering.' Much of it is hands-on building: experimental infrastructure, owning performance of RL runs, and diagnosing training instabilities. However, it also requires 'a track record of original technical work in ML training or systems, such as new methods, architectures, or optimizations' and asks the hire to 'develop next-generation model architectures and RL algorithms.' That is a novel-research expectation, which puts the role in a borderline zone. Level is the deciding factor. Level: The posting does not state an explicit year count ('Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements') and does not require a PhD. Even so, the minimum qualifications clearly target senior frontier-scale practitioners: deep familiarity with large-scale transformer training dynamics, hands-on experience training large models in a distributed setting with data/tensor/pipeline parallelism tradeoffs, ownership of end-to-end performance of Anthropic's largest RL runs down to the hardware, and a track record of original technical work. The $500,000-$850,000 salary band confirms a senior or staff level. Ananya is a new grad finishing an MS in CS (AI concentration) at Boston University in 2026-12. Her experience is one 8-month ML Engineer co-op (a RAG prototype and fine-tuning a small transformer classifier tracked with MLflow) and a solo coursework project on RAG chunking strategies. She has no distributed or large-scale training experience and no record of original methods or architectures. This is not a realistic new-grad level, so the role fails the level test. Skills: The required section names Python, JAX, and PyTorch. Python and PyTorch are in her shipped list, so the narrow skills test technically passes. But the core requirement is distributed large-model training at scale, and nothing she has shipped covers it; Ray, her nearest distributed-compute tool, is only in familiar_with_not_shipped. Location: San Francisco, New York City, and Seattle are US offices with a 25% in-office hybrid policy, and she is willing to relocate within the US, so location passes. Sponsorship: The posting says 'We do sponsor visas!' with best-effort caveats and no disclaimer, so it passes her needs_sponsorship requirement. Research Engineer is in her target_roles, and location and sponsorship pass, but the explicit senior-level expectations put this out of reach for a new grad. Verdict: NOT_RELEVANT.
